entries.title: Proverbs 14:2
segments: 2. uprightness--is the fruit of fearing God, as falsehood and ill-nature (
) of despising Him and His law.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:3
segments: 3. rod of pride--that is, the punishment of pride, which they evince by their words. The words of the wise procure good to them.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:4
segments: 4. crib is clean--empty; so "cleanness of teeth" denotes want of food (compare
). Men get the proper fruit of their doings (

5. A faithful witness, &c.--one tested to be such. 
 
    utter lies--or, "breathe out lies"--that is, habitually lies (
; compare

segments: 6. An humble, teachable spirit succeeds in seeking (

entries.title: Proverbs 14:7
segments: 7. Avoid the society of those who cannot teach you.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:8
segments: 8. Appearances deceive the thoughtless, but the prudent discriminate.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:9
segments:
9. Fools make a mock at sin--or, "Sin deludes fools." 
 
    righteous ... favour--that is, of God, instead of the punishment of sin.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:10
segments: 10. Each one best knows his own sorrows or joys.

segments: 13. The preceding sentiment illustrated by the disappointments of a wicked or untimely joy.

segments: 14. filled ... ways--receive retribution (

entries.title: Proverbs 14:17
segments: 17. He ... angry--literally, "short of anger" (compare

entries.title: Proverbs 14:18
segments: 18. inherit--as a portion (compare

entries.title: Proverbs 14:19
segments: 19. Describes the humbling of the wicked by the punishment their sins incur.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:20
segments: 20. This sad but true picture of human nature is not given approvingly, but only as a fact.

entries.title: Proverbs 14:21
segments: 21. For such contempt of the poor is contrasted as sinful with the virtuous compassion of the good.
